classic-laddie's nightly `cosmo-rebuild` converge loop has been failing every run since ~Jul 22 (machine is frozen on the Jul 19 generation) because the ONLY broken package, `ollama-cuda`, fails to compile: `make: *** [Makefile:136: all] Error 2` in its vendored llama.cpp build. This derivation is a dependency of system-path -> the whole nixos-system-classic-laddie toplevel, so one package failure blocks the entire generation switch.

ROOT CAUSE (already diagnosed, no need to re-investigate): cosmo's nixpkgs input tracks the nixos-unstable channel, currently locked at rev e2587caef70c1e63e5faf82f5f9d269e13860b45 (nixos-unstable HEAD, 2026-07-23 08:54 UTC), which ships ollama 0.32.1. That version shipped with a MISMATCHED vendored llama.cpp source and does not build. Upstream nixpkgs fixed it ~8h later on master in commit ffc8c1c9eb5b8fa3cac1e7d5c23505a244ad8971 ('ollama: 0.32.1 -> 0.32.3', immediately followed by 'add update.sh which also updates llamaCppSrc'). As of now BOTH nixos-unstable AND nixpkgs-unstable channels are still frozen/behind and do NOT yet contain the fix (nixos-unstable is 236 commits behind ffc8c1c); only master has 0.32.3. e2587ca is a clean ancestor of ffc8c1c (0 ahead / 236 behind), so moving to ffc8c1c is a pure forward jump with the SMALLEST possible nixpkgs delta that still includes the fix.

TASK: In flake.nix (line ~8), change the nixpkgs input from tracking the branch to pinning the fix commit:
  from: nixpkgs.url = "github:nixos/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable";
  to:   nixpkgs.url = "github:nixos/nixpkgs/ffc8c1c9eb5b8fa3cac1e7d5c23505a244ad8971";
Add a comment above it explaining WHY and the revert condition, e.g.:
  # TEMP PIN (2026-07-25): nixos-unstable is frozen at e2587ca which ships a
  # broken ollama 0.32.1 (vendored llama.cpp mismatch, fails to build). Pinned
  # forward to the master rev that carries the ollama 0.32.3 fix (nixpkgs
  # ffc8c1c9eb). REVERT to github:nixos/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable once that channel
  # advances past the 0.32.3 bump.
Then run `nix flake lock` (or `nix flake update nixpkgs`) to regenerate flake.lock. All other inputs use follows=nixpkgs so they move with it — that's fine.

CRITICAL — WHY THE .url MUST CHANGE (not just the lock): .github/workflows/update-flake-lock.yml runs nightly at 00:00 and AUTO-MERGES its PR (gh pr merge --auto --squash), and CI only does `nix build ... --dry-run` for the hosts, which never actually compiles ollama and so passes even when the build is broken. If you leave nixpkgs.url pointing at nixos-unstable and only edit the lock, tonight's job will `nix flake update` nixpkgs back to the frozen broken rev, dry-run CI will pass, it will auto-merge, and classic-laddie breaks again. Pinning an explicit rev in .url makes `nix flake update` a no-op for nixpkgs, so the fix survives.

VERIFY (this is the whole point — CI will NOT catch a build failure because it is dry-run only): on this host, actually BUILD the real toplevel, do not use --dry-run:
  nix build .#nixosConfigurations.classic-laddie.config.system.build.toplevel --no-link -L
Confirm ollama-cuda builds to 0.32.3 and the toplevel completes. You are running on classic-laddie itself (AMD 5950X, has the GPU, nix binary caches, and the existing store) so this is expected to take a while for the ollama-cuda CUDA compile — that is normal, let it finish. Also run `nix flake check` and, at minimum, `nix build .#nixosConfigurations.makers-nix.config.system.build.toplevel --dry-run` and the same for johnny-walker to confirm the other hosts still evaluate under the bumped nixpkgs. Confirm the resulting store path is named nixos-system-classic-laddie-...ffc8c1c (not e2587ca).
